n: Paul opens forcefully: his apostleship came neither from any human source nor through human appointment, but from Jesus Christ and the Father who raised Him. Critics in Galatia had questioned his authority.

f.w: not of men, neither by man

n: He writes with the brethren traveling with him to the congregations of Galatia, a region in central Asia Minor (modern Turkey).

f.g: Likely the congregations Paul founded in towns like Antioch of Pisidia, Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe.

n: His usual blessing of grace and peace from the Father and the Son.

f.w: Grace be to you and peace

n: Christ gave Himself for our sins to rescue us from this present evil age, as the Father willed. The Atonement is front and center from the first lines.
To God be glory forever.

f.g: Literally “to the ages of the ages.”

n: Skipping his usual thanksgiving, Paul expresses shock that they are so quickly turning from God, who called them by Christ’s grace, to a different “gospel.”

f.g: Quickly deserting — like a soldier defecting.

n: There really is no other gospel. Some people are troubling them, trying to distort the gospel of Christ — teachers who insisted Gentile converts be circumcised and keep the law of Moses.
Even if Paul or an angel from heaven preached a different gospel, let that one be accursed. The message matters more than the messenger.
He repeats it for emphasis: anyone preaching another gospel than the one they received stands under God’s curse.

f.g: He had warned them during his visits.

n: Is Paul trying to win human approval or God’s? If he were still pleasing people, he couldn’t be Christ’s servant.

f.w: do I seek to please men?

n: He assures them the gospel he preached did not originate with any human.
He didn’t receive it or learn it from people, but by revelation from Jesus Christ.

f.w: by the revelation of Jesus Christ

n: They know his past: as a zealous Jew he violently persecuted God’s Church and tried to destroy it.
He outpaced many his age in Judaism, being extremely zealous for the traditions of his ancestors.

f.g: The oral traditions of the Pharisees.

n: But God set Paul apart even before birth and called him by grace — echoing Jeremiah’s call.

f.w: separated me from my mother's womb

n: God revealed His Son to Paul so he could preach Christ to the Gentiles. Paul didn’t immediately consult anyone.
He didn’t go to the earlier apostles in Jerusalem; he went into Arabia and then returned to Damascus.

f.g: Probably the Nabataean kingdom east and south of Damascus.

n: Three years later he went to Jerusalem to get acquainted with Peter, staying fifteen days.

f.g: Greek historeo — to visit to get to know or inquire.

n: The only other apostle he met then was James, the Lord’s brother.
Before God, Paul declares he is not lying — showing how seriously his independence was being challenged.
Next he went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia, including his hometown, Tarsus.

f.g: A region in southeast Asia Minor; Tarsus was its chief city.

n: The congregations in Judea didn’t know him personally.
They only heard that their former persecutor now preached the faith he once tried to destroy.
And they praised God because of the change in Paul. A transformed life is a powerful witness.
